verdict.rationale: The CLI exposes a `mint export` command explicitly described as producing a static site export for air-gapped/self-hosted deployment, and Mintlify also supports fully self-hosting the platform on AWS/Kubernetes, giving developers a documented path to escape SaaS lock-in. However, this is only confirmed via a CLI probe rather than first-party docs detailing export fidelity, and community commentary explicitly criticizes Mintlify as proprietary/SaaS-locked (users choosing MkDocs instead over lock-in concerns), tempering confidence that this is a mainstream, well-documented workflow. Missing for 10: first-party documentation detailing what `mint export` produces and its completeness/fidelity, and independent confirmation that an exported bundle can be hosted elsewhere without loss of functionality.
